title: The Borrowed Verdict Again
premise: Ines Voss, the town's coroner for thirty years, receives a confession letter claiming that Ada Kessler — buried a week earlier as a suicide — was murdered by her own family to secure an inheritance. The letter is postmarked the day after Ada's funeral and signed with Ines's own name, a name he never wrote. As the anniversary dinner of Ada's late husband approaches, Ines quietly reopens the case, discovering the confession was dictated by Ada herself before she died. At the dinner, Ines reveals the truth: Ada poisoned herself slowly and framed her heirs, testing whether anyone loved her enough to look past the verdict; her granddaughter, who alone investigated, inherits everything.
about_author: S. M. Okonkwo is the pen name of a former court clerk who spent a decade transcribing small-town inquests before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the quiet violence hidden inside respectable families.

chapters.title: Postmarked Grief
chapters.summary: Ines Voss's POV. A week after signing off on Ada Kessler's suicide verdict, Ines receives a confession letter in his own handwriting describing her murder. Shaken, he exhumes his notes and finds his signature page subtly forged. The emotional beat is professional pride curdling into doubt: the man who knows every grave by name no longer trusts his own record.

chapters.title: The Heirs' Table
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, intercut with the granddaughter Mara's journal entries. Ines interviews the three heirs under the guise of routine paperwork, mapping their alibis and resentments around the inheritance. Mara, suspicious of his questions, begins her own inquiry. The beat is rising tension as every answer fits too neatly, suggesting the family rehearsed a story together.

chapters.title: What the Body Kept
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Toxicology on retained tissue samples shows slow arsenic dosing over months — self-administered or not, someone controlled Ada's food. Ines confronts the housekeeper, who admits Ada dictated the confession letter and paid her to mail it after the funeral. The climax builds as Ines realizes the dead woman orchestrated her own investigation from beyond the grave.

chapters.title: A Glass Raised
chapters.summary: Ines's POV at the anniversary dinner. Before the toast, he lays out the truth: Ada poisoned herself to expose which heir would grieve her and which would merely wait. Only Mara had questioned the verdict — loyalty proven through doubt rather than obedience. The estate passes to her; Ines closes the case he swore was closed, at peace with justice outside the law.
